clinician.final_diagnosis: Ovarian schistosomiasis caused by Schistosoma mansoni
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 45-year-old female from schistosomiasis-endemic Pernambuco, Brazil with a history of river bathing approximately 10 years prior presented in mid-2014 with strong left iliac pain. Endovaginal ultrasound (September 2014) revealed enlargement of the left ovary (2.84 cm cyst, volume 16.82 cm³, normal range 3.0–9.0 cm³). MRI confirmed an enlarged left ovary with neoplasia not excluded. Tumor markers tested in October 2014 were normal. Left ovariectomy was performed in April 2015. Histopathological examination of the resected ovarian tissue identified ovarian schistosomiasis with granulomatous inflammatory processes surrounding both viable and calcified eggs of S. mansoni, accompanied by lymphoplasmacytic and eosinophilic infiltrates, multinucleated giant cells, epithelioid macrophages organized in palisades, and fibroblast hyperplasia with incipient fibroplasia. Parasitological examination using the Kato-Katz method performed in April 2016 confirmed residual S. mansoni infection with egg loads of 60, 192, and 156 eggs per gram of feces. The patient received anthelmintic treatment with praziquantel 50 mg/kg (4.5 tablets of 600 mg each), with two additional treatments administered at two-month intervals to address the ectopic form of the disease.
